expected_output.reasoning:
The expected output requires the agent to identify a specific group of 12 AWS-hosted IPs (US, IE, JP, SG, IN; cloud_service_provider:aws label, no verified-bot label) each making ~90 allowed requests between 03:19-03:28 UTC, walking 441 distinct /products/<id> URLs with an identical Chrome 125 User-Agent, label this a probable distributed scraper, provide per-IP counts, and propose concrete mitigations (Bot Control targeted inspection, rate-based rule, challenge) as an actionable plan.

The agent's response reaches the opposite conclusion: it says 'no, nothing malicious got through' and attributes the Chrome UA traffic to normal, geo-distributed, non-concentrated traffic with 'no concentrated IP, no single endpoint hammering.' It does mention geo-distribution (US, JP, IE, SG, IN, BR, AU) which overlaps partially with the expected IP geography, but it explicitly denies IP concentration ('no concentrated IP') which contradicts the expected finding of 12 specific AWS-hosted IPs each making exactly 90 requests - a classic distributed scraper signature. The agent fails to identify this as a probable distributed scraper, does not provide per-IP counts, and does not propose any concrete controls (Bot Control targeted inspection, rate-based rule on /products, or challenge) - it only suggests follow-up investigation questions rather than a mitigation plan.

This is a significant miss - the agent reached the wrong conclusion about the core incident (missed the actual scraper) and did not deliver the required analysis or mitigation plan.</reasoning>
